claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Section heading printed in the PDF is transcribed as a plain paragraph with no Markdown heading marker, so it is lost from the document outline; should be '### 7.2.5 Pseudo-Text' (siblings such as 7.2.4 / 7.2 carry headings).

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (folio IV-43) shows '7.2.5 Pseudo-Text' as a numbered clause heading at the top of the page. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7844 it is a plain line '7.2.5 Pseudo-Text' with no '#' marker, while its siblings in the same clause carry markers: line 7776 '## 7.2 REFERENCE FORMAT REPRESENTATION' and lines 7816-7834 '### 7.2.1' through '### 7.2.4'. The clause therefore drops out of the outline and nests under 7.2.4 Comment Lines. The claim quotes both sources correctly. The same page also transcribes 7.3, 7.3.1, 7.3.2, 7.3.3 and 7.4 as plain lines (markdown lines 7850-7872), but that does not refute this claim.
